I've farmed this land 40 years, so I mostly do what worked last year. 60 mu is a lot — I can't afford to try too many new things.

Here's how I split the ground: 25 mu goes to winter wheat then summer maize double-crop (that's my main income, wheat sells okay and maize feeds good). 20 mu is spring peanut — peanut price has been fair and the soil here takes peanut well. The other 15 mu I keep in cotton like my father did, though cotton is tiring work.

For fertilizer I buy compound fertilizer (三元复合肥) and urea at the town dealer. I don't weigh everything — I go by bags per mu, same as neighbors.

**Wheat:** I put about 2 bags compound (15-15-15) per mu at sowing, plus about 15 kg urea top-dress at jointing. That's roughly 18 kg N, 7-8 kg P, 7-8 kg K. I water 3 times — winter, jointing, filling. Well water is there but electricity costs money. Spray 2 times for aphids and rust. Improved variety, same seed I buy every year. Expect around 480 kg/mu.

**Summer maize:** After wheat I rotary till and plant right away, no time. Use 1.5 bags compound at sowing, then 20 kg urea at big-trumpet stage. Hybrid seed — everyone uses hybrid now. Water 2 times if no rain. Spray 1-2 times for borer. Expect 550 kg/mu.

**Spring peanut:** Peanut is legume so less nitrogen — 1 bag compound (15-15-15) is enough, maybe add some potassium because peanut likes K. Plough deep before planting, that matters for peanut. Improved variety. Water 2 times, spray 2 times for leaf spot. Expect 320 kg/mu (shelled).

**Cotton:** Cotton eats fertilizer. 2 bags compound at base, then 15 kg urea at flowering, another 10 kg at boll. Hybrid seed, Bt type so less bollworm spray but still spray 4-5 times for aphids and spider mites. Water 3 times. Plough the field. Expect 250 kg/mu lint.

I'd rather put a little extra fertilizer than short the crop — losing yield hurts more than the fertilizer cost.
